segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, um, hi everyone.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So this is our first meeting, the kickoff meeting.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I'm Helen, I'll be the project manager for this one.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Um, maybe we can just go round and say who we are?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, sure. I'm Rafael, I'm the industrial designer.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I'm Nadia, um, marketing expert.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Tomasz. User interface design.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Great. Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So, the project. Uh, we're designing a voice-controlled kitchen timer.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: The idea is you can set it and check it just by talking to it, so you don't have to touch it while you're cooking.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So like, hands covered in flour, that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Exactly, yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And management wants it to be original, trendy and user-friendly. Those are the three words they keep using.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Very specific.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So the plan is we have four meetings. This one, then functional design, conceptual design, and then detailed design.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And in between you'll each work on your own bit and get emails from, uh, the coach.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Before we get into it, um, they want us to try out the whiteboard.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So everyone draw their favourite kitchen gadget. Quickly.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Oh, um—

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'll go first, fine.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That's... a garlic press. That's supposed to be a garlic press.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: It looks like a stapler.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: It's a very aggressive garlic press.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, mine is a whisk. Which is basically just lines.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: And I've done a toaster, because it's the only thing I can draw.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Lovely. Okay, we're all artists. Moving on.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So, budget.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Um, the selling price is going to be thirty-five euros.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Sorry, I mean twenty-five. Twenty-five euros selling price.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And the production cost can't be more than twelve fifty per unit.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Twelve euros fifty?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Twelve fifty, yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And the target is fifty million euros profit, um, internationally.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: That's a lot of timers.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: That's a lot of pasta.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Right, so we'll just make it out of solid gold and sell four of them then.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Ha, yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Uh, let's maybe not.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: No, so twelve fifty is the ceiling, so we do have to keep the parts pretty cheap.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, no, that's fair. Voice recognition isn't free though.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, so let's just get some first ideas going. What do people think a voice timer needs?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Well, um, from the marketing side, I think the big thing is people cook more than one thing at once.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Like rice on one ring and something in the oven.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So multiple timers. You'd say 'pasta timer, ten minutes' and 'oven timer, forty'.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, exactly that.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, I like that.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: How many though? Because each one has to show up somewhere.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I mean, it doesn't have to be loads. Three, four?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Mm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And you name them, so it can say 'the pasta is done' instead of just beeping.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Ooh, that's nice.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Does everyone agree we want it to handle more than one timer at a time?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Definitely.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, so that's in. Multiple timers, we'll work out the number later.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Uh, one thing I'm worried about is noise.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Kitchens are loud. Extractor fan, stuff frying, the radio on.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So it has to actually hear you.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, and that's microphone quality, which is cost again.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Maybe it could have a button as backup? Like if it doesn't hear you.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Hmm, but then it's not really voice controlled.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: No, but like a backup. For when it's really loud.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I think that's worth thinking about, but let's not decide now.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I can look into what microphones we can actually afford.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, that'd be good.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, what about a wake word? Like 'hey timer'. Otherwise it'll go off every time someone says 'minutes'.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Ha, yeah, that would be annoying.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Makes sense. Let's say it'll have a wake word.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Wake word is pretty standard on the chips anyway, I think.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And then maybe we connect it to a phone app, so you can see the timers from the living room.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Hmm. Does that fit in twelve fifty though?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Bluetooth or wifi, that's probably a stretch.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, okay, fair.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Let's park the app idea for now.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Oh, and maybe a magnet on the back so it sticks on the fridge.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That's cheap, at least.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Or a stand, or—

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Um.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: We can come back to that kind of thing in the conceptual meeting.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Who's it for, actually? Like, who are we selling to?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: The brief just says home cooks, so pretty broad.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay, I could do a bit of research on that. What people actually want from a kitchen timer.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yes, that's basically your job for next time.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, so, for the next meeting.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Rafael, you'll look at the working design, so the components, what's inside it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah. Including the microphone stuff.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Tomasz, you'll do the technical functions design, so what it actually has to do and how people talk to it.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, sure.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And Nadia, user requirements, so what users want.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And I'll write up the minutes from this and send them round.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: When's the next one?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: In about thirty minutes. You'll get an email with more specific instructions.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Any questions before we finish?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Just to check, twenty-five is the selling price, yeah?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Twenty-five, yeah. Ignore the thirty-five, my mistake.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay, cool.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And we're not doing the gold one.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: We are not doing the gold one.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Shame.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay. Thanks everyone.

abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, the team members introduced themselves, and the project manager presented the project: a voice-controlled kitchen timer that is original, trendy and user-friendly and can be operated hands-free while cooking.
The team tried out the whiteboard by drawing their favourite kitchen gadgets.
The project manager presented the budget: a selling price of 25 euros, a maximum production cost of 12.50 euros per unit, and a profit target of 50 million euros.

In a first round of ideas, the team agreed the timer should support multiple simultaneous timers and use a wake word, and discussed kitchen noise, a backup button, a phone app and a fridge magnet without settling them.
The project manager assigned individual preparation tasks for the functional design meeting, which follows in about thirty minutes.
actions: The industrial designer will work on the working design, including what microphones are affordable.
The user interface designer will work on the technical functions design.
The marketing expert will work on user requirements, including research on what home cooks want from a kitchen timer.
The project manager will write up and distribute the minutes.
decisions: The timer will support more than one timer running at a time; the exact number is still to be determined.
The timer will use a wake word.
problems: Kitchen noise may stop the timer from hearing users, and a good microphone adds cost within the 12.50 euro limit.
Whether to add a backup button for loud situations was left open.
A phone app connection was parked as probably too expensive.
A fridge magnet or stand was left for the conceptual design meeting.
The number of simultaneous timers is undecided.
The target group is broadly defined as home cooks.

The selling price is 25 euros (initially misstated as 35 euros and corrected).
The production cost must not exceed 12.50 euros per unit.
The profit target is 50 million euros internationally.
The timer will support multiple simultaneous timers, with the number to be decided later.
The timer will use a wake word.
The user interface designer suggested three or four named timers that announce which one is done.
The marketing expert suggested a backup button for when it is too loud; it was left undecided.
The user interface designer suggested connecting the timer to a phone app; it was parked over cost concerns.
The marketing expert suggested a magnet on the back to stick it on the fridge; it was deferred to the conceptual design meeting.
The target group in the brief is home cooks.
The industrial designer will work on the working design, including affordable microphones.
The user interface designer will work on the technical functions design.
The marketing expert will work on user requirements and research what users want.
The project manager will write up and send round the minutes.

edge_cases.note: The industrial designer jokes that they'll just make it out of solid gold and sell four; the project manager dismisses it and restates the 12.50 cost ceiling, and it is not adopted.
The project manager says the selling price is thirty-five euros, then immediately corrects it to twenty-five euros and confirms twenty-five later.
